answer: With k bonded identities, correlated equivocation exposes up to k(k−1)/2 culpable pairs, so base penalties scale as O(k²). Detection also applies asymmetric depreciation: the loss multiplier grows as e^(λk), λ>0, against the swarm’s escrowed capital. Splitting stake across aliases therefore does not dilute shared risk; each identity adds exposure. A jetty of separate accounts cannot shelter the kernel of coordination, even when the swarm appears to be an oasis of independent operators.
